summary.intent: Resolve all open PR review comments on the phase-39 branch (user-configurable vault parameters), then address a follow-up request to clean up a now-redundant bin store retention days write path.
summary.outcome: All 11 review threads across two rounds resolved (7 + 4), all fixes committed and pushed, lockfile pinned to axios 1.13.2, and the dead retentionDays field fully removed from bin.store.ts.

repo: Phase 39 branch is docs/phase-39-context; phase 38 was docs/phase-38-context.
PR #423 is the active PR for phase 39 (user-configurable vault parameters).
TEE IPNS key enrollment follows the StorageTab pattern — wrap key with teePublicKey before calling createAndPublishIpnsRecord.
vault-ipns.test.ts had a pre-existing @cipherbox/core circular import issue that was already fixed on docs/phase-38-context (commit 560c871fe) but hadn't been merged into phase 39.
retentionDays in bin.store.ts was dead write-only state — all reads had already moved to useVaultSettingsStore after the phase 39 useBin.ts refactor.
pnpm lockfile had YAML formatting churn (inline vs expanded blocks) from a main merge; only real content difference was axios specifier ^1.13.2 → 1.13.2 (security pin).
A poisoned axios version was published on 2026-03-31; axios was manually pinned to 1.13.2 in the lockfile.
recycleBinRetentionDays min was changed from 1 to 0 (allow indefinite retention disabled), per D-03 spec requirement.

code.finding: Minimum recycleBinRetentionDays was clamped to 1; changed to 0 to allow disabling recycle bin retention per D-03.
Test 'should clamp recycleBinRetentionDays below 1 to 1' was asserting old min=1 behavior; updated to expect 0 after min change.
retentionDays now sourced directly from useVaultSettingsStore, making useBinStore.setRetentionDays calls redundant.
setTimeout without cleanup on unmount; fixed with useRef + cleanup function in useEffect.
retentionDays field and setRetentionDays setter removed entirely — no remaining consumers after useBin.ts refactor.
Missing TEE enrollment before createAndPublishIpnsRecord; added teeKeys wrapping following StorageTab pattern.
New test file created (not added to vault-ipns.test.ts) to avoid the pre-existing @cipherbox/core import resolution failure in that file.
JSDoc range comment said 1-365; updated to 0-365 after min change.

workflow: When a branch is missing commits from a sibling branch (not yet merged to main), cherry-pick or manually apply the fix rather than waiting for a full merge.
When resolving merge conflicts in pnpm-lock.yaml resulting from different pnpm YAML serialization styles, running pnpm install regenerates the canonical format.
Grep for all consumers before removing a store field — write-only dead state can accumulate without type errors if the setter signature is still valid.
CI failures on review-fix branches often come from pre-existing tests asserting old behavior that the fix intentionally changes — check test files alongside source files.

friction: vault-ipns.test.ts had a pre-existing @cipherbox/core circular import failure that blocked running new tests in the same file, requiring a separate test file.
The fix for the circular import was on docs/phase-38-context but not yet on docs/phase-39-context, requiring a manual forward-port.
Main merge caused ~15k lines of YAML formatting churn in pnpm-lock.yaml, obscuring the only real change (axios version pin).
Three merge conflicts had to be resolved manually after merging main: ROADMAP.md, vault-ipns.test.ts, and useBin.ts.
STATE.md was overwritten by the merge with main's stale phase-38 state and had to be manually restored.
CI caught the vault-settings.test.ts regression (min=1 assertion) only after push — should have been caught locally before the first commit.
open_items: Preset quick-select UI in VaultTab (VaultTab.tsx:203) was marked 'not applicable' as a deliberate simplification — may need to be implemented in a future phase.
pnpm-lock.yaml formatting churn from the main merge was left as-is (squash merge to main will resolve it) — may want to run pnpm install on main periodically to keep format canonical.
axios 1.13.2 is pinned as a security measure; the pin should be revisited once a clean non-poisoned version is published and verified.
useBinStore still exists with other fields (items, etc.) — the retention cleanup is done but the store itself could be audited for other stale patterns in a future cleanup.
